navy:
GERMANY (deu) — surface fleet, all six eras. Measured under jsc against clean HEAD (a62fcc9), loadouts resolved AFTER generations.js, not read off the source line.

16 surface hulls: 6 destroyers (Z-1 Fletcher e50, Lutjens Type 103 e60, Bremen F122 e80, Brandenburg F123 e90, Sachsen F124 e00, Sachsen F124 e20), 3 corvettes (Koln Type 120 e60, K130 e00, K130 Batch 2 e20), 4 missile boats (Type 148 Tiger e60, Type 143 Albatros e80, Type 143A Gepard e90, Gepard late e00), 2 torpedo boats (Jaguar e50, Zobel e60), 1 mine hunter (Frankenthal Type 332, e90 onward). Plus the four faction-agnostic `both` hulls every navy shares (navminelayer, minesweeper, lst, oiler, repair_sea, all from e50).

Zero carriers, zero cruisers, zero nuclear ships, zero SSBNs — measured, not assumed, and CORRECT. Zero naval land-attack weapons — also correct as an intent, though five hulls quietly inherited tgt.ground 1 from shared NATO/French rounds.

THE HEADLINE: of 16 German surface hulls across six eras, only THREE carried any anti-air weapon and only two of those a missile, and both of those are e20. Every era row from 1958 to 2008 is a ONE-WEAPON stub inheriting an American weapon id. The Lutjens — Germany's first area air-defence ship — had tgt.air 0. The Sachsen F124 at e00 — the brief's own test case, "an excellent air-defence ship and the game should show it" — carried a single Mk 45 127 mm gun and nothing else, while the desc on the same line names "SM-2, ESSM, RAM and Harpoon" and explicitly says the 127 mm belongs to the Type 125, not this ship. The Brandenburg carried one weapon literally named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha" — the Arleigh Burke's name, truncated at 42 characters, claiming a Tomahawk Germany has never owned, behaving as a gun. That is the prompting defect reproduced exactly, on a German frigate.

Structural cause: every e50-e00 naval row in eras.js for gbr, fra and deu points at the generic w_<era>_nato_<role> weapon. The defect is fleet-wide; this audit fixes Germany's share of it.

Proposed fix: 19 edits, all tested. 13 new German naval rounds in rules.js, 13 era rows repointed, 3 e20 rows corrected, one truncated desc completed, one quality multiplier corrected. After it, every German surface combatant from 1961 onward has the air defence and ASW it really had; no German ship carries an American or French weapon it never had; and no German ship carries a land-attack missile.

TGT-MASK SUMMARY, measured across the whole German surface fleet:
 - Can engage AIR: 3 of 16 (deu_e60_corvette and deu_e00_corvette via a dual-purpose gun; corvette_g and destroyer_g via RAM/SM-2). Lutjens, Bremen, Brandenburg, Sachsen e00, both Gepards, the Fletcher and the Frankenthal: all tgt.air 0.
 - Can engage SUB: 2 of 16, and both are torpedo boats (deu_e50_patrol, deu_e60_patrol) using the shared generic `torpedo`. Not one German frigate or destroyer in any era can attack a submarine, despite sonar values up to 8.0 and despite every one of those hulls carrying Mk 32 324 mm tubes or Bofors 375 mm in reality.
 - Claim tgt.ground 1 with a MISSILE (i.e. naval land attack): 5 of 16 — deu_e60/e80/e90_missileboat, deu_e00_missileboat, corvette_g. Germany has never had one.
 - vls / helo / radarQ fields: ZERO German hulls carry any. The NAVY refit table in rules.js covers nato, pla, pact, kpa and roc only.
 - ciws_ gun weapon: zero German hulls. CORRECT — Germany never bought Phalanx.

findings.whatTheGameHas: ONE weapon: "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" [g1a0s1u0] dmg119 rng11.0. tgt.air = 0. No SAM, no anti-ship missile, no ASW. Germany's only air-defence hull cannot engage an aircraft.
findings.whatIsReal: F219 Sachsen, commissioned 4 November 2004, three ships. APAR (four fixed X-band active phased-array faces) plus SMART-L; 1x 76 mm OTO Melara; 32-cell Mk 41 with 24 SM-2 Block IIIA and 32 ESSM quad-packed into 8 cells; 2x RAM Mk 49 21-cell; 8x RGM-84 Harpoon in two quads; 2x Mk 32 triple 324 mm with MU90; two Sea Lynx Mk88A. The row's own desc says "SM-2, ESSM, RAM and Harpoon beneath it" and then says the 127 mm gun is what the Type 125 has and why the Type 125 "cannot do this job at all" — the game gave the Sachsen the Type 125's gun and took away everything the desc names.
findings.fix: Replace the single gun with navgun_76, sam_sm2, sam_ram, a German anti-ship Harpoon and asw_mu90. Edit 15.

findings.whatTheGameHas: ONE weapon named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha" — 42 characters, truncated mid-word — resolving as proj=shell, aoe 0.9, [g1a0s1u0]. It is w_e90_nato_destroyer, the USS Arleigh Burke's entry, inherited whole. A German frigate advertising 96 Mk 41 cells and Tomahawk, firing a gun, unable to shoot at an aircraft.
findings.whatIsReal: F215 Brandenburg, commissioned 14 October 1994, four ships. 1x 76 mm OTO Melara Compatto; Mk 41 with SIXTEEN self-defence-length cells carrying RIM-7M Sea Sparrow — not SM-2, the cells are too short; 2x RAM Mk 49, the first German class designed with RAM from the drawing board; 4x MM38 Exocet; 2x twin Mk 32 324 mm; two Sea Lynx Mk88A. Germany has never possessed a Tomahawk or any other naval land-attack missile. The row's own desc says "Sea Sparrow in a vertical launcher and two RAM mounts".
findings.fix: Replace with deu_navgun_76c, deu_sam_seasparrow, sam_ram, deu_ssm_mm38, deu_asw_mk46. Edit 12.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Eight RGM-84 Harpoon" [g1a0s1u0] dmg196 rng12.5 — the USS Pegasus hydrofoil's loadout, w_e80_nato_missileboat.
findings.whatIsReal: P6111 Albatros, commissioned 1976, ten Type 143 boats: FOUR MM38 Exocet, TWO 76 mm OTO Melara Compatto fore and aft, two 533 mm stern tubes with DM2A1 Seeaal, mine rails. No German fast attack craft ever carried a Harpoon of any mark. The row's own desc says "four MM38 Exocet each" and "The 143A traded the after 76 mm gun for a RAM launcher position".
findings.fix: Replace with deu_ssm_mm38, deu_navgun_76c, deu_flak_40. Edit 11.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "RGM-84 Harpoon" and nothing else. No RAM. The unit's `full` field is literally "Gepard (P6121), Type 143A with RIM-116 RAM" and its entire desc is about RAM — "among the first ships in the world to carry it" — and the weapon list has no air-capable weapon at all.
findings.whatIsReal: Type 143A: 4x MM38 Exocet, 1x 76 mm OTO Melara forward, 1x RAM Mk 49 21-cell aft in place of the after 76 mm. RAM became operational in 1992 and these boats were first with it, which is exactly what the desc says and exactly what the loadout denies.
findings.fix: Replace with deu_ssm_mm38, deu_navgun_76c, sam_ram. Edit 13.

findings.whatTheGameHas: ssm_exocet = "MM40 Exocet Block 3" [g1a0s1u0] dmg250 rng14.4, sole weapon. service:"2008".
findings.whatIsReal: The Type 143A carried MM38 Exocet from commissioning in 1982-84 until the last three boats paid off in November 2016 — MM40 Block 3 is a 2010s round with a land-attack mode that Germany never fitted to a Gepard. No Gepard was commissioned in 2008 either; the service field asserts a date that never happened. And the boat still has no RAM and no gun.
findings.fix: Replace with deu_ssm_mm38, deu_navgun_76c, sam_ram. Edit 14. The service date is flagged but not edited — see risks.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Two 127mm/54 Mk 42" and nothing else. tgt.air = 0. Germany's first area air-defence ship cannot shoot at an aircraft.
findings.whatIsReal: D185 Lutjens, commissioned 22 March 1969 at Bath Iron Works, three ships (Lutjens 1969, Molders 1969, Rommel 1970). Charles F. Adams hull with German modifications: two 127 mm/54 Mk 42, one Mk 13 single-arm launcher with RIM-24B Tartar (later RIM-66 SM-1MR), one Mk 112 ASROC octuple launcher, two Mk 32 triple 324 mm tubes. The row's own desc names "Tartar, ASROC and two 127 mm" and calls them "the first real air-defence ships Germany ever had".
findings.fix: Keep the gun — it is correct — and append deu_sam_tartar and deu_asw_asroc. Edit 8.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Two 127mm/54 Mk 45" [g1a0s1u0], sole weapon. tgt.air = 0.
findings.whatIsReal: F207 Bremen, commissioned 7 May 1982, eight ships on a Dutch Kortenaer hull. ONE 76 mm OTO Melara Compatto — the class never carried a five-inch gun of any kind; 8x RGM-84A Harpoon in two quad launchers; one Mk 29 octuple launcher with RIM-7M Sea Sparrow from commissioning; two twin Mk 32 324 mm with Mk 46; two Sea Lynx Mk88. RAM came only in the 1990s, which the row's desc already states correctly. The desc names "Harpoon, Sea Sparrow, two Sea Lynx and a 76 mm" — four systems, none of them present.
findings.fix: Replace with deu_navgun_76c, deu_sam_seasparrow, deu_ssm_harpoon84a, deu_asw_mk46. Edit 10.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "One 127mm/54 Mk 42" — an American automatic mount the class never had.
findings.whatIsReal: F220 Koln, commissioned 1961, six ships, the first warships designed and built in Germany after the war. Two 100 mm Creusot-Loire Model 1953, six 40 mm Bofors L/70, TWO 375 mm Bofors four-barrel ASW rocket launchers, four 533 mm ASW tubes. The row's own desc names "two 100 mm French mountings and two 375 mm Bofors anti-submarine rocket launchers".
findings.fix: Replace with deu_navgun_100, deu_flak_40, deu_asw_bofors375. Edit 7.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts" [g1a0s1u0], tgt.air 0.
findings.whatIsReal: Z-1 (D170) is ex-USS Anthony (DD-515), a wartime Fletcher transferred in 1958. Fletchers carried FIVE 127 mm/38 calibre Mk 30 single mounts, a dual-purpose gun with a real anti-aircraft role. The Mk 42 is a 1953 automatic mount that first went to sea in USS Forrest Sherman (DD-931, 1955) and then the Charles F. Adams — it was never fitted to a Fletcher. Wrong count, wrong calibre length, wrong mount, wrong decade, and the DP capability denied.
findings.fix: Give Germany its own deu_navgun_127_38 with tgt.air 1. Edit 5. NOTE the shared weapon stays correct for its owner nato_e50_destroyer (Forrest Sherman really did have three Mk 42); gbr_e50_destroyer and fra_e50_destroyer inherit it and are equally wrong, out of scope here.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "One 57mm Mk 110" — the Bofors gun of the American Littoral Combat Ship — as the sole weapon. No RAM, no anti-ship missile.
findings.whatIsReal: F260 Braunschweig, commissioned 2008. One 76 mm OTO Melara Super Rapid, two 27 mm MLG 27, two RAM Mk 49 21-cell launchers, four RBS15 Mk3, mine rails. The row's own desc names "a 76 mm, two RAM launchers and four RBS15".
findings.fix: Replace with navgun_76, sam_ram, ssm_rbs15. Edit 16.

findings.whatTheGameHas: ssm_exocet = "MM40 Exocet Block 3", the French round, on the German corvette. Both this row's desc and the e00 row's desc say RBS15.
findings.whatIsReal: The K130 has carried RBS15 Mk3 (Saab, built in Germany by Diehl) since 2008 across both batches; Germany ordered RBS15 Mk4 in 2022. It has never carried an Exocet of any mark. The Mk3 is also the ONE anti-ship round in German naval service with a genuine land-attack mode, so it is the one German round that honestly keeps tgt.ground 1.
findings.fix: Swap ssm_exocet for a new ssm_rbs15 in rules.js. Edit 2.

findings.whatTheGameHas: navgun_76, sam_sm2, sam_ram. No anti-ship missile and no ASW weapon. Germany's only ocean escort cannot engage a ship or a submarine, while the American destroyer_n carries ssm_harpoon and asw_mk54 and the British corvette_b carries asw_stingray.
findings.whatIsReal: The Sachsen carries 8x RGM-84 Harpoon in two quad launchers and two Mk 32 triple 324 mm tubes firing MU90 Impact — asw_mu90 already exists in the weapon table and is the correct German round.
findings.fix: Append a German anti-ship Harpoon and asw_mu90. Edit 3.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Two MM38 Exocet anti-ship missiles" and no gun. tgt.ground 1 on the missile.
findings.whatIsReal: Twenty craft built by CMN Cherbourg to a German requirement, first commissioned 1972. FOUR MM38 Exocet, one 76 mm OTO Melara Compatto forward, one 40 mm Bofors L/70 aft. The game already knows this: js/warship_specs.js line 63 describes this exact unit as "76 mm OTO turret forward, four Exocet canisters in two staggered pairs amidships, 40 mm on the stern" and gives it guns:1, gunCal:76. The 3D model spec and the weapon table disagree and the model is right.
findings.fix: Replace with deu_ssm_mm38 (four rounds, ground 0), deu_navgun_76c, deu_flak_40. Edit 9. Desc also truncated — Edit 18.

findings.whatTheGameHas: navgun_57 = "57mm naval gun", the shared generic MCMV gun.
findings.whatIsReal: M1066 Frankenthal, commissioned 1992, twelve ships. One 40 mm Bofors L/70 (later replaced by 27 mm MLG 27) plus Stinger, and the Seehund and Pinguin mine-disposal drones. The class has never carried a 57 mm. This is the one hull in the German roster whose branch the codebase itself calls world-leading — rules.js says "Mine countermeasures is the one branch of naval warfare where Germany genuinely leads" — and it is carrying the wrong gun.
findings.fix: Replace navgun_57 with deu_flak_40. Edit 4.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Both: "12.7mm HMG" [g1a0s1u0] dmg13 plus the generic heavyweight torpedo.
findings.whatIsReal: Forty Jaguars from 1957 and ten Zobels from 1962, both Lursen-built, both with TWO 40 mm Bofors L/70 and four 533 mm torpedo tubes. The Jaguar's own desc says "two 40 mm and four torpedo tubes". A Bofors L/70 is an anti-aircraft gun; a 12.7 mm HMG with tgt.air 0 is not, so the game also strips these boats of their only air defence.
findings.fix: Replace hmg with deu_flak_40 on both. Edits 6 and 7 (patrols).

findings.whatTheGameHas: Measured: the German Sachsen's SM-2 resolves to acc 0.791 against the American Arleigh Burke's 0.900 — the identical missile. German RAM resolves to 0.774 against a base table value of 0.880. The comment justifies 0.72 with "no carrier, no cruiser, no long-range naval strike".
findings.whatIsReal: All three justifications are ROSTER facts already modelled by absence: the German list contains no carrier hull, no cruiser hull and no land-attack round, so the game charges for them once already. Charging a second time as accuracy makes German-built systems worse than American ones at the things Germany builds — and RAM is a German requirement, developed with the United States, that went to sea on the German Type 143A in 1992 before anyone else had it, as rules.js's own comment states. 0.72 is the same figure given to the Warsaw Pact and Taiwan.
findings.fix: Raise to 0.90 — still below nato and gbr at 1.00, level with France — and rewrite the comment to say the gap is scale and reach, not build quality. Edit 19. OPTIONAL: it also moves the German submarines, which another workflow owns.

findings.kind: land attack — right intent, wrong table
findings.unit: five German hulls: deu_e60/e80/e90_missileboat, deu_e00_missileboat, corvette_g
findings.whatTheGameHas: Every one of them carries an anti-ship missile with tgt.ground 1 inherited from a shared NATO or French round, which quietly gives the Bundesmarine a naval land-attack capability in four of six eras.
findings.whatIsReal: No German surface warship has ever carried a land-attack missile — no Tomahawk, no MdCN, no SCALP Naval, no Kalibr equivalent. The only German naval fire that has ever reached a shore target is a gun. The one honest exception is RBS15 Mk3 on the K130, which really does have a land-attack mode.
findings.fix: All new German anti-ship rounds get tgt.ground 0; ssm_rbs15 alone keeps ground 1 with a comment saying why. Built into edits 1, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16.

findings.whatTheGameHas: desc is 320 characters and ends mid-word: "...the Bundesmarine's entire concept of operations depended o".
findings.whatIsReal: A generator truncation. The same artefact shows in the weapon names: about fifty weapon names in the eras.js JSON block sit at exactly 42 characters, including "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha" (missing "wk") which is the one that lands on the Brandenburg.
findings.fix: Complete the sentence with the boat's real armament. Edit 18. The 42-character weapon-name truncation is fleet-wide and out of scope here; removing it from the German hull is enough for this audit.

findings.whatTheGameHas: minesweeper_g starts at e90. Germany has no national mine warfare hull in e50, e60, e80 or e00, and no minelayer hull ever.
findings.whatIsReal: Type 320 Lindau, eighteen coastal minesweepers from 1957; the Troika system of 1981, one manned Type 351 control boat directing three unmanned Seehund drones, the first operational unmanned minesweeping anywhere; Type 343 Hameln from 1989. Minelayers: Type 457 Sachsenwald (A1437) 1968 and Steigerwald (A1438) 1969. Germany's mine rails also ran on the Type 143/143A and run on the K130.
findings.fix: NOT edited. The faction-agnostic `both` hulls navminelayer and minesweeper are available to Germany from e50 and cover the function; this is a texture gap, not a capability gap. Recording it so the owner can decide.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Zero German hulls carry vls, helo or radarQ. The NAVY refit table in rules.js covers nato, pla, pact, kpa and roc only — gbr, fra and deu hulls all get none. The comment on that table calls helo "the single biggest ASW multiplier".
findings.whatIsReal: Sachsen: 32 Mk 41 cells and two helicopters. Brandenburg: 16 cells and two helicopters. Bremen: two Sea Lynx. Koln: none. Lutjens: none.
findings.fix: NOT edited — it is a game-wide structural gap affecting three European navies equally, not a German identity defect, and fixing it for Germany alone would misrepresent the comparison.

findings.kind: realism over symmetry — absences that are right
findings.whatTheGameHas: Measured: zero units with role carrier, cruiser, ssbn or ssgn in any era. No corvette in e50, e80 or e90. No missile boat in e50 or e20. No patrol boat after e60. No nuclear surface ship. No naval land-attack weapon.
findings.whatIsReal: Every one of these is correct. Germany has never had a carrier, a cruiser, a nuclear surface ship or a naval strategic weapon. The Koln class paid off between 1982 and 1989 and nothing replaced it until the K130 in 2008 — the deu_e60_corvette desc states this and the roster honours it exactly. The Bundesmarine had no anti-ship missile of any kind until Exocet arrived on the Type 148 in 1972 — the Zobel desc states this and there is correctly no e50 missile boat. The last Gepard paid off in November 2016 — the corvette_g desc states this and there is correctly no e20 missile boat.
findings.fix: None. Leave every one of these absences exactly as it is. This is the realism-over-symmetry rule already applied correctly and it should be recorded as checked and sound.

findings.whatTheGameHas: No ciws_ gun weapon on any German hull in any era, while nato, pla, pact and roc hulls all carry one.
findings.whatIsReal: Germany never bought Phalanx or any gun CIWS for its escorts. RAM is the German close-in weapon — a German requirement co-developed with the United States, first to sea on the Type 143A in 1992 — and it is what fills that role on the Bremen (retrofit), Brandenburg, Sachsen and K130. The absence is the right answer.
findings.fix: None. Recorded as checked and sound.

findings.kind: shared weapon that is genuinely shared
findings.whatTheGameHas: "Two 127mm/54 Mk 42" shared with nato_e60_destroyer (USS Charles F. Adams).
findings.whatIsReal: The Lutjens IS a Charles F. Adams — three hulls built at Bath Iron Works to the American design with German modifications, carrying the same two Mk 42 mounts. This is the one case in the German era rows where inheriting the American weapon is exactly correct, and the fix keeps it.
findings.fix: None — kept unchanged in edit 8, which only appends Tartar and ASROC.

risks: COLLISION WITH A PARALLEL WORKFLOW — edit 19 only. Raising DOMAIN deu naval from 0.72 to 0.90 in generations.js also moves every German SUBMARINE (deu_e50_sub through sub_g), which the non-American submarine audit owns. Edit 19 is separable and marked optional; edits 1-18 touch nothing below the waterline. If the submarine workflow has its own view of that multiplier, drop edit 19 and keep the rest.

THE SCRATCHPAD IS SHARED, NOT SESSION-PRIVATE. Other workflows are writing into /private/tmp/.../scratchpad and overwrote my probe files mid-run; one early measurement came back showing British weapons (sam_seaslug, asw_limbo, ssm_exocet38) that do not exist at HEAD, because a parallel gbr workflow had the working tree transiently patched when I copied it. Everything reported here was re-measured from an isolated `git archive HEAD` export in DEU_SURF_AUDIT_9931 with unique filenames. Anyone re-running this should do the same.

A gbr surface workflow appears to be adding its own MM38 Exocet as `ssm_exocet38`. My `deu_ssm_mm38` is a separate id with German figures, so the two coexist without conflict — but if both land, the owner may want to note that the same missile now has two entries, which is correct (different navies, different fits) but worth knowing.

ssm_rbs15 is added WITHOUT rows in rules.js MISSILE_PROFILE and MISSILE_SPEED, carrying profile, intercept and speed inline instead. That is deliberate and tested — the fall-through loop at the foot of rules.js skips anything that already has .profile — but if someone later adds an ssm_rbs15 row to those tables it will silently override the inline values.

ROLE NAMES ARE GAME ROLES, NOT NAVAL RATES. Koln (role corvette) and Bremen, Brandenburg and Sachsen (role destroyer) are all frigates. I did not touch the role fields: changing them would move units between build menus and tech tiers for no gain in realism, and the `full` field already states the true type on every row.

SIGHT VALUES MOVE AS A SIDE EFFECT. The 'eyes to match the reach' pass in generations.js raises a unit's sight to cover its longest weapon, so adding a 14.6-tile RBS15 to deu_e00_corvette lifts its sight from 9.0 to 14.7. This is the existing mechanism working as designed — corvette_g already sat at 15.2 for the same reason — but five German hulls do see further after the fix.

deu_e00_missileboat service:"2008" asserts a Gepard commissioning that never happened (the class commissioned 1982-84). I flagged it but did NOT edit it, because the e90 sibling deliberately uses 1992 for the RAM fit rather than the build date and I could not tell whether the e00 row is following that same documented convention or is simply wrong. Worth an owner decision.

I did not verify that the AI's target selection uses the full weapons array rather than weapons[0] for naval units. The behaviour suite passing and the e20 hulls already carrying three to five weapons each is strong evidence it does, but I did not read the acquire path in ai.js to confirm it, so the practical effect of the appended SAMs and ASW rounds in live play is inferred rather than observed.
